clue.text: Hairstyle with another flipping English flower

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the second hairstyle is read back to front

blocks.note: a DA (short for duck's arse) is a slicked-back 1950s hairstyle
another hairstyle: hair wound into a knot at the back of the head
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone sports one fancy hairdo alongside another, with an English bloom tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second hairstyle. 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is anything that flows, and the Danube is one of Europe's great rivers.

clue.text: What cellist's cleaner might do left in depressed part of US?

blocks.note: a cleaner tidying a cellist's things might wipe down the bow
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a cellist's housekeeper, set in some sunken corner of America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dust Bowl was the drought-stricken region of the 1930s US prairies; 'depressed' plays on both its economic misery and a low-lying bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dust Bowl was the area of the American Great Plains ruined by drought and poverty in the 1930s Depression.

clue.text: Knight on silver horse

blocks.note: N is the knight in chess notation
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A knight mounted on a silver-grey steed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Short human entertaining Dadaist composer

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter is dropped
to entertain is to host, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a human being
Max Ernst, the German Dada and Surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A small person amuses an avant-garde music writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The human loses its last letter, then the Dadaist painter slips in after its first letter, an unusually early split point.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was the American composer of West Side Story and a celebrated conductor.

clue.text: A perfect order is a fruit tart

blocks.note: first meaning: as in the idiom for complete neatness
second meaning: a pastry dessert filled with baked apples

explanation.surface: Ordering a flawless dessert at the bakery counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in apple-pie order' means perfectly tidy, so the answer stands for the order on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'apple-pie order' means perfect neatness, and the same words name a baked apple pastry.

clue.text: Trap attractive letter writer for Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial consonants change places

blocks.note: fit is British slang for attractive, and a pen pal writes letters

explanation.surface: A warning that a charming correspondent may be luring someone into a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is British slang for sexy or attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a concealed hole for catching animals, hence any hidden danger or trap.

clue.text: A fastening device put up a vine

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a nail fastens things together

explanation.surface: Someone nails up a climbing plant to hold it in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Great male ape on exotic tree

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big male gorilla sits up in a foreign tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomegranate is a small fruit-bearing tree as well as its seed-filled fruit.

clue.text: Bury Hospital Department given eminent award by Bishop

blocks.note: Ear, Nose and Throat department
the Order of Merit, a distinguished British honour
B is the bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A hospital unit receives a top honour from a bishop, read like a news headline from the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town heading a news item, but it is the verb. The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour limited to 24 living members.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, so it is a synonym for burying.

clue.text: Courage beer found in this?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for nerve or guts
second meaning: the glass container that holds beer

explanation.walkthrough: Courage is also a British beer brand, so the clue seems to be about where that beer is kept; 'bottle' is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for nerve, and a bottle is also the glass vessel that beer is sold in.

clue.text: Candy bow found in Western river

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it, so one piece goes into the other
heading west in an across clue means reading right to left

blocks.note: arco is the musical direction to play with the bow
the Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A sweet tied with ribbon turns up in a river out west.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is turned round to SUGAT and ARCO sits inside it. 'Candy' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to coat in sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: To candy something is to preserve or glaze it in sugar, which is exactly to sugarcoat it.

clue.text: Reveal a senior manager switched pcs etc

indicators.note: two things switched have swapped places, so the pair of letters runs the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
managing director
computers fall under information technology

explanation.surface: An executive confesses that they swapped out the office computers.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to own up to it, which is to reveal or confess it.

clue.text: Took care of a minor issue

definitions.text: Took care of a minor issue

blocks.clueFragment: Took care of a minor issue
blocks.note: surface reading: dealt with a small problem
setter's reading: a minor is a child, and issue means offspring, so this is minding a young child

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor issue' sounds like a small problem, but issue means offspring and minor means underage, so the caring was childminding.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after someone's young child while the parents are out is what a childminder did.

clue.text: Family love something on which to cook fruit

blocks.note: blood relations are family
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a range is a cooking stove

explanation.surface: Relatives fondly gather around the stove to cook some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' belongs with the range: something on which to cook is a range, a kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood orange is a citrus fruit with deep red flesh.

clue.text: Asian priest returned to school compound

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A Buddhist monk goes back to his old school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, a gam. 'Compound' looks like an enclosure; it is a mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend, especially of mercury with another metal, so a compound in the broad sense.

clue.text: Doctor left home-brewed ale unfinished with a part of healthy diet?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
taken as written before losing its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A GP has left some half-drunk home brew, part of a supposedly healthy regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person who prescribes a healthy diet, but it is the verb meaning tamper with. Ale shortened gives AL before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from wholemeal flour is a staple recommended in a fibre-rich healthy eating plan, so it is one component of it.

clue.text: Avoid more complicated type of flick

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a film genre with a needlessly convoluted plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A road movie is a film genre about a journey, and flick is slang for a film.

clue.text: Eject drunk sot in plane sitting at the front

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: a jet is an aircraft
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly drunk passenger on an aircraft is thrown off, perhaps from a front-row seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting at the front' places the aircraft first, before the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw cargo overboard or cast something off, so it means to eject.

clue.text: Suspect one might be recognised here

definitions.text: Suspect one might be recognised here

blocks.clueFragment: Suspect one might be recognised here
blocks.note: surface reading: a vague guess that someone would be known in some place
setter's reading: suspect is a noun, the accused person picked out by a witness in a police line-up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as the verb 'I suspect', but it is the noun: a crime suspect being picked out of a line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British name for a police line-up, where witnesses try to pick out the culprit.

clue.text: Troublemaker takes stories to press

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous creature
lore is a body of traditional tales

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker sells tales to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers, but it is the verb meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore someone is to beg or urge them earnestly, which is to press them.

clue.text: Wise, say, to include aristo in annual

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the preceding word is taken by its sound
including something means holding it within, so the nobleman goes inside

blocks.note: spoken, the word sounds like the plural of the letter Y
an earl is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: Comedian Ernie Wise hosts a nobleman in a yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like Ernie Wise of Morecambe and Wise, the British comedy double act; it is read as the sound of two letter Ys.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yearly happens once each year, so the adjective is a synonym of annual.

clue.text: Stretch then follow devoted supporter

blocks.note: a lap is a stretch of a race
to dog someone is to trail them

explanation.surface: A fan who stretches out and then tags along everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is figuratively a slavishly loyal follower, someone utterly subservient.

clue.text: Displays with it need approval from CAA

definitions.note: a description of what the answer requires, not a synonym

blocks.note: to air something is to show it
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Trendy shows need sign-off from the regulator.
explanation.walkthrough: The CAA is the Civil Aviation Authority, the UK body that licenses aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is an aircraft, so it needs certification from the aviation regulator before flying.

clue.text: Animal has endless hunger within

within means inside, so one word sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its last letter
a yen is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: A beast is consumed by never-ending hunger.

clue.text: A specialised soldier on the way to give support

Royal Marines, a specialist fighting force
re means on or concerning
abbreviation for street

clue.text: Girl one leaves is thick

blocks.note: a girl's name
Roman numeral one

clue.text: It's clear that around 50 I can be forgetful!

blocks.note: obvious means plain or clear
Roman numeral fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits wryly that hitting fifty brings memory lapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means being unaware or unmindful, close to forgetful of one's surroundings.

clue.text: Not even rum?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes numbers that are not divisible by two and also anything peculiar or strange.

clue.text: What many pensioners have upstairs is something hard to define

second meaning: an ambiguous situation not clearly fitting any category

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstairs' is slang for the head, so the first meaning is a patch of grey hair rather than a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an indeterminate zone between categories, and literally a patch of grey on an older person's scalp.

clue.text: Blush wine and a joint

blocks.note: red wine
a joint is a seedy place, a den

explanation.surface: Someone flushes after a glass of wine and a puff on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette or a cut of meat, but here it is a dive or hangout.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to go red in the face, which is to redden.
